scenarios.name: ball_catch
scenarios.verification: BOTH sides now navigate the real battle bag. Until 2026-08-12 the port gate preset wCurItem/wWhichPokemon/wPseudoItemID and called UseItem directly while the golden side navigated ITEM -> MASTER BALL for real, so the two sides reached the same outcome by different routes and the port's menu leg was never executed. 2c ported BagWasSelected / DisplayBagMenu / UseBagItem, so the bypass was replaced by an AUTOKEY_ITEMBALL press sequence through the production DisplayBattleMenu; the gate asserts wBattleResult == 2 (only .returnAfterCapturingMon sets it) before dumping. The committed golden was NOT regenerated -- the port converged onto the existing one, and dropping a single DOWN from the press table makes the run produce no dump at all. State verification, not UI verification

scenarios.name: battle_anim_physical
scenarios.verification: Stage 6 physical move-animation witness: a real wild-battle FIGHT -> STRENGTH turn, stopped at DrawFrameBlock's first published live OAM frame. The reference watches for a CHANGE from parked battle-menu OAM rather than merely nonzero OAM, so the compared unmasked OAM entries cannot be stale menu state. The port reuses DEBUG_BATTLE_FAINT's faithful ExecutePlayerMove entry and dumps at the matching projection boundary before the faint path cleans OAM.

scenarios.name: battle_anim_elemental
scenarios.verification: Stage 6 elemental move-animation witness, the twin of battle_anim_physical: a real wild-battle FIGHT -> THUNDERSHOCK turn stopped at DrawFrameBlock's first published live OAM frame. The reference watches for a CHANGE from parked battle-menu OAM rather than merely nonzero OAM, so the compared unmasked OAM entries cannot be stale menu state. The shared debug party carries no elemental move, so BOTH sides pin wBattleMonMoves+3 to THUNDERSHOCK and leave its PP alone; wBattleMon therefore still compares clean. Unlike the physical twin this checkpoint sits on the subanimation/flash path.

scenarios.name: battle_anim_blink
scenarios.verification: Stage 6 shake/blink witness, the first of the family whose landmark is not a frame block. After a move's own animation MoveAnimation calls PlayApplyingAttackAnimation, which dispatches on wAnimationType; type 4 (player used a damaging move without a side effect, which STRENGTH selects) is BlinkEnemyMonSprite -> AnimationBlinkMon, six hide/show iterations. Both sides stop at the FIRST hidden-pic instant, pinned by TWO conditions: the enemy's 7x7 pic block at GB (12,0) is blank AND enemy HP is still nonzero -- damage is applied only after MoveAnimation returns, so full HP separates a blink hide from any later hide. Sits strictly between battle_anim_physical (stops earlier, inside the move animation) and battle_faint (stops after the KO), a gap nothing had covered.

scenarios.name: battle_anim_optoff
scenarios.verification: Stage 6 animations-OFF witness, the last of the family. With wOptions BIT_BATTLE_ANIMATION set, MoveAnimation skips ShareMoveAnimations and PlayAnimation for a flat 30-frame delay (engine/battle/animations.asm:437-446). THE LANDMARK IS INSIDE THAT DISABLED ARM, and that is the point: an earlier version stopped at battle_anim_blink's shared hidden-pic landmark and PASSED while proving nothing, because the only surfaces separating the animated route from this one there are 79 VRAM tile slots (49..127) and the wOptions byte, and every one of those slots is inside _BATTLE_VRAM_MASKS_MENU ($8000-$87FF). A port that ignored the option would still have passed. Stopping inside the arm fixes that BY CONSTRUCTION: the port must take the arm to dump at all, so a port that animated anyway never reaches the checkpoint and the run fails loudly rather than green. The reference stops at the matching ROM instant -- the move-used message fully printed with the enemy pic still up -- which is true only inside the delay window; nothing moves during those 30 frames, so the state is static and the sides need not agree on a frame number.

scenarios.name: battle_anim_ball
scenarios.verification: Stage 6 ball move-animation witness. Same landmark as its physical/elemental siblings -- DrawFrameBlock's first published live OAM frame -- but entered through the real battle ITEM menu (ITEM -> MASTER BALL) rather than FIGHT. It exists because ball_catch (id 20) cannot witness this: that scenario is datastruct/WRAM-only and dumps only after wBattleResult goes 2, by which point every toss frame block has been cleaned up. The animation under test is ULTRATOSS_ANIM ($C6), which is what pret selects for a MASTER BALL (engine/battle/animations.asm:2795) -- NOT TOSS_ANIM ($C1). The party is still 5 at the dump, which is what distinguishes this instant from ball_catch's post-capture one.

scenarios.name: battle_faint
scenarios.verification: synthetic-port-gate plus real-navigation golden; state verification, not UI verification. FIRST scenario in which a battle turn resolves and a mon faints: before it no scenario reached the damage pipeline or the faint/EXP chain

scenarios.name: battle_blackout
scenarios.verification: synthetic-port-gate plus real-navigation golden; state verification, not UI verification. The other half of battle_faint's coverage: battle_faint kills the ENEMY, this one kills the PLAYER, so RemoveFaintedPlayerMon and HandlePlayerBlackOut execute for the first time. Building it found a real defect: ReadPlayerMonCurHPAndStatus was a no-op, so the fainted mon's 0 HP never reached the party and the battle looped faint->resend forever

scenarios.name: battle_switch
scenarios.verification: the FIRST scenario in the registry that presses PKMN. Both sides drive the real 2x2 battle menu (RIGHT then A) into the real party menu and take SWITCH, so PartyMenuOrRockOrRun, SwitchPlayerMon, RetreatMon and AnimateRetreatingPlayerMon execute for the first time -- battle plan 2a and 2b both landed with zero execution evidence behind this gap. Neither side calls SwitchPlayerMon directly: a harness that duplicates the production sequence inherits production's bug and cannot witness its own fix. Compared surface is the switch's WRAM outcome, above all wBattleMon holding the NEW mon (PERSIAN L80) fully sent out. No roll is involved: no move is used and no damage is dealt before the dump

scenarios.name: battle_item_potion
scenarios.verification: the FIRST scenario that opens the in-battle BAG. ball_catch does not count: its gate presets wCurItem and calls UseItem directly, bypassing the whole menu leg battle plan 2c ported, so BagWasSelected, DisplayBagMenu and UseBagItem had no execution evidence at all. Both sides drive the real menus (DOWN+A to ITEM, A on POTION, A on the party target). It found a real defect on its first run: GetItemName dropped pret's `.Finish: ld de, wNameBuffer`, so UseBagItem's CopyToStringBuffer read from a flat name-table pointer and the port page-faulted the moment an item was chosen. Compared surface is the heal arithmetic (seeded HP + 20, no roll anywhere) and the consumed bag slot

scenarios.name: battle_choose_next_mon
scenarios.verification: the FORCED SWITCH: the third door out of HandlePlayerMonFainted and the only one nothing had opened. battle_faint kills the ENEMY, battle_blackout kills the player's LAST mon; this one kills the player's mon with another alive, so AnyPartyAlive succeeds and DoUseNextMonDialogue + ChooseNextMon run for the first time (battle plan 2b landed both with zero execution evidence). Both sides drive the real menus: YES to "Use next POKeMON?", then the party cursor to slot 5. The dump is STATE-GATED on both sides rather than return-based, because on this path HandlePlayerMonFainted ends in `jp MainInBattleLoop` and never returns -- the landmark is wPlayerMonNumber == 5 AND wLoadedMon species == LAPRAS, which is after SendOutMon's DrawPlayerHUDAndHPBar so wLoadedMon needs no mask

scenarios.name: battle_item_no_effect
scenarios.verification: the only scenario that takes an item's FAILURE path: a POTION on a FULL-HP mon, so ItemUseMedicine reaches .healingItemNoEffect -> ItemUseNoEffect. battle_item_potion covers the success path. The dump is STATE-GATED on both sides rather than return-based, because on failure UseBagItem is `jp z, BagWasSelected` (pret core.asm:2360-2362) and DisplayBattleMenu never returns -- the landmark is wCurItem == POTION AND wUsedItemOnWhichPokemon == 1 AND wActionResultOrTookBattleTurn == 0, the last being the failure edge since UseItem_ sets it to 1 on entry. Target is slot 1, not slot 0, because 0 is cleared WRAM and would not distinguish 'failed' from 'never ran'. What is compared is that NOTHING happened: the bag still holds 16 entries with POTION x1 and every party HP is untouched

scenarios.name: battle_pay_day
scenarios.verification: the ONLY scenario that enters EndOfBattle's Pay Day payout branch, which is gated on wTotalPayDayMoney != 0 and therefore dead in every other scenario -- battle plan 3b stood implemented-but-unticked for want of it. SNORLAX L80 uses PAY_DAY on the spec wild PIDGEY L13 through the real FIGHT menu; the KO ends the battle and EndOfBattle pays out with AddBCD. BOTH SIDES SEED wPlayerMoney TO 001000 FIRST: measured, the debug seed leaves it at the BCD maximum 999999, where AddBCD saturates and the payout would leave the compared bytes unchanged -- the scenario would pass while proving nothing. Expected end state 001160, i.e. level*2 = 160, which is RNG-free; the damage roll only decides whether the KO happens and PAY_DAY at power 40 from L80 overkills 36 HP on every roll

scenarios.name: battle_wrap
scenarios.verification: the ONLY scenario in which CheckNumAttacksLeft clears a SET bit. Its two call sites are both in MainInBattleLoop's turn tail and neither is reachable from ExecutePlayerMove, so this is the first harness on either side that lets the real MainInBattleLoop run turns. SNORLAX L80 wraps the spec wild PIDGEY L13; the scenario-local rows wPlyStatus1 and wPlyAtksLeft pin the release. Three pins, each measured: enemy HP 999 because a KO takes `jp z, HandleEnemyMonFainted` and skips the turn tail entirely; enemy asleep because its damage to SNORLAX is a roll and wBattleMon is compared; and the trapping counter forced to 1 because TrappingEffect rolls it 2-5 and the emulators do not share an RNG stream

scenarios.name: battle_self_destruct
scenarios.verification: the MUTUAL FAINT: FaintEnemyPokemon's .sfxplayed player-also-fainted arm, which battle_faint (enemy only) and battle_blackout (player only) cannot reach. THE DUMP INSTANT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN and took three attempts. Both sides dump in the ONLY observable window: wBattleResult == 1 with both HP words 0. That byte is written ONLY by RemoveFaintedPlayerMon, which in this flow runs ONLY on that arm, and FaintEnemyPokemon RE-ZEROES it a few instructions later (pret core.asm:825-826), so it is caught per frame during the text and pic-slide. Two earlier versions dumped after FaintEnemyPokemon returned; both passed their diff AND their sabotage, i.e. proved nothing -- party slot 0's HP reaches 0 either way, wBattleResult is re-zeroed, and wPartyGainExpFlags is consumed by the EXP distribution. Deterministic by construction: ExplodeEffect zeroes the USER's HP with no accuracy test and a power-130 hit from L80 overkills 36 HP on every roll

scenarios.name: battle_damage
scenarios.verification: semantic numerical oracle: a non-critical Pikachu THUNDERSHOCK and a critical PIDGEY SLASH are non-lethal; each emulator's independently sampled result must match the canonical Gen-1 base, STAB, type-effectiveness and 217..255 random-factor arithmetic

scenarios.name: trainer_battle_route
scenarios.verification: the CONTINUOUS overworld->battle->return scenario, and the only one in which the port's real OverworldLoop drives a trainer battle end to end: sight engagement by the map script, entry through the loop's own wCurOpponent poll, the live battle menus, and the .battleOccurred return that dispatches EndTrainerBattle. 44/45/46 call StartTrainerBattle and InitBattle from a harness and never run the loop, so none of them can prove this. Compared surface is choreography (battle result, wIsInBattle, wCurOpponent cleared, map-script indices, the persistent beaten flag, the .battleOccurred status-flag work, map and coords) plus the two zero-RNG reward bytes (player money BCD, lead mon EXP). Damage and HP are deliberately NOT compared: pinning them would require RNG lockstep through live menu timing, and per-turn damage math is already covered by battle_faint and 45/46

scenarios.name: battle_exp_all
scenarios.verification: the Exp. All whole-party branch of FaintEnemyPokemon, which no scenario had ever entered because the seeded bag holds no EXP_ALL. Both sides pin item 15's id to EXP_ALL (wBagItems + i*2 -- the LIST, no +1; wNumBagItems is the separate count byte) so the bag compares clean. The branch halves wEnemyMonBaseStats and runs GainExperience a SECOND time over the whole party; the golden's dump landmark is the LAST party slot gaining EXP, which only the whole-party pass credits, so a run that silently fell back to the fought-mon-only path fails instead of passing. Reaching it is what exposed the DivideExpDataByNumMonsGainingExp runaway loop fixed in 17d670c2f -- that routine is unreachable without Exp. All. Deterministic by matchup, exactly as battle_faint: STRENGTH's minimum roll overkills PIDGEY's 36 HP and SNORLAX outspeeds it, and each mon's share is a function of base EXP, level and the number of mons gaining EXP, never a roll

scenarios.name: battle_bide
scenarios.verification: the Bide STORE and RELEASE — ExecutePlayerMove's .bideCheck accumulating and .unleashEnergy clearing STORING_ENERGY, zeroing the accumulator and dealing twice what was stored. battle_wrap witnessed the TRAPPING counter; nothing had ever set STORING_ENERGY. Like battle_wrap this needs the REAL MainInBattleLoop, because Bide only means anything across two turns. Four pins, each measured: enemy HP 999 so the release does not KO, enemy asleep because Bide accumulates the damage the USER TAKES and an enemy turn would put a roll straight into the compared accumulator, the rolled counter forced to 1 so the release lands on the same turn on both sides, and the accumulator forced to 100 (with wDamage zeroed alongside it) so the release is a real one rather than .unleashEnergy's degenerate wMoveMissed arm. All the mid-battle writes are gated on STORING_ENERGY being SET, which is what guarantees they cannot land between the release computing wDamage and HandleIfPlayerMoveMissed applying it. Landmark: the enemy at 999-2*100 = 799 HP, having SEEN STORING_ENERGY set — the latch matters because bit-clear-and-accumulator-zero is also the pre-battle state

scenarios.name: battle_thrash
scenarios.verification: the END of a thrash — ExecutePlayerMove's .thrashingAboutCheck clearing THRASHING_ABOUT and setting CONFUSED once the rolled counter runs out. battle_wrap witnessed USING_TRAPPING_MOVE and battle_bide witnessed STORING_ENERGY; nothing had ever set THRASHING_ABOUT. Needs the REAL MainInBattleLoop, like both of those, because the block only means anything across two turns. THE ENEMY HP PIN IS 65535, NOT battle_wrap's 999, and that was measured: THRASH is power 90 against WRAP's 15, so two hits go through 999 and the thrash ends by KO instead of by the routine — a failure that reads exactly like the feature being broken. What is compared is the state transition (THRASHING_ABOUT clear + CONFUSED set + counter 0) behind a latch proving the bit was seen SET, since not-thrashing-and-not-confused is how the battle starts. wPlayerConfusedCounter is carried as a row but SKIPPED: it is a second BattleRandom roll, and pinning it would make the comparison a tautology

scenarios.name: battle_oldman
scenarios.verification: DisplayBattleMenu.doSimulatedMenuInput -- the old-man / Prof. Oak tutorial menu, the first scenario to execute it. Compares wPlayerName, already a STANDARD region: pret copies NAME_LENGTH=11 from the 8-byte .oldManName literal, so the correct bytes are 8E 8B 83 7F 8C 80 8D 50 8F 91 8E -- "OLD MAN" @ plus the adjacent "PRO" of .profOakName -- and a port padding with 0x50 differs in exactly the last three (the defect fixed in dbe6e797b). THE STAGING IS THE POINT: a special battle NEVER sends out the player's mon (pret StartBattle core.asm:171) and never enters MainInBattleLoop (it loops on DisplayBattleMenu, core.asm:176), so wBattleMon stays ZERO throughout on both sides. The harness sets wBattleType before the send-out decision rather than in the gate body, which is what makes the two sides agree

scenarios.name: battle_oldman_result
scenarios.verification: The RESULT/EXIT half of the per-battle-type box for OLD_MAN: battle_oldman (id 69) stops at the rename inside the menu, this follows the same battle to its end. Landmark is wBattleResult == 2, the same one ball_catch polls -- pret's UseBagItem.returnAfterCapturingMon (core.asm:2393-2399) sets wBattleResult=2 and scf together, and .displaySafariZoneBattleMenu is `call DisplayBattleMenu / ret c`, so a capture exits the battle early and the SAFARI tail after it is reached only when carry is CLEAR. BOTH SIDES LAND POST-TEARDOWN (the port gate calls EndOfBattle before dumping) because the window where wBattleResult reads 2 while wIsInBattle is still 1 is only a few frames wide and the reference's A-taps step past it. SENSITIVITY, MEASURED not predicted: forcing the port to skip .oldManCaughtMon (so the tutorial takes the NORMAL catch path) makes this scenario FAIL -- on `wEnemyMon party pos, want $00 got $0D`. Note wPartyData MATCHED under that sabotage, so the sabotaged port did not actually gain a party mon; the discriminator is the enemy party-position field, not party/dex as first designed. PIN NOTE: unlike battle_oldman this scenario pins the enemy with SLEEP ONLY on both sides -- battle_oldman's 65535-HP pin outlives the battle here and showed up as a one-field divergence in whichever direction it was applied asymmetrically.

scenarios.name: battle_pikachu_result
scenarios.verification: The RESULT/EXIT half for BATTLE_TYPE_PIKACHU, the twin of battle_oldman_result (id 79). battle_pikachu (id 70) stops at the rename inside the menu; this follows the same battle to its end. DisplayBattleMenu dispatches OLD_MAN and PIKACHU to the SAME .doSimulatedMenuInput and ItemUseBall routes BOTH to .oldManCaughtMon (item_effects.asm:529-532) -- caught but not handed to the player -- so the same wBattleResult == 2 landmark and the same pins apply. Both sides land POST-TEARDOWN (the port gate calls EndOfBattle before dumping) because the pre-teardown window is only a few frames wide, and both pin the enemy with SLEEP ONLY -- battle_pikachu's 65535-HP pin outlives the battle at this instant and is %ifndef'd out of the RESULT gate. NON-VACUITY, MEASURED: its golden is BYTE-IDENTICAL to battle_oldman_result's -- expected, since hardware reaches the same terminal state for both types once the tutorial name is restored -- so the value is that it exercises the PORT's PIKACHU path. Proved distinct: sabotaging ONLY the PIKACHU arm of ItemUseBall's tutorial check makes THIS scenario FAIL while battle_oldman_result still PASSES.

scenarios.name: battle_pikachu
scenarios.verification: battle plan 4a's must-hit Pikachu-battle scenario. Same .doSimulatedMenuInput as battle_oldman -- DisplayBattleMenu dispatches BATTLE_TYPE_OLD_MAN and BATTLE_TYPE_PIKACHU to it identically (pret core.asm:2094-2098) -- so what this adds is the OTHER name. It witnesses the half battle_oldman structurally cannot: str_profoak_name's 11-byte tail is pret CODE (FA 2D, the first two bytes of ld a,[wBattleAndStartSavedMenuItem]) rather than the data-adjacency the old-man tail is, and the generator's warning that those bytes drift if upstream edits handleBattleMenuInput had no enforcement before this. wBattleMon stays ZERO on both sides throughout: a special battle never sends out the player's mon (pret StartBattle core.asm:171) and never enters MainInBattleLoop (it loops on DisplayBattleMenu, core.asm:176)

scenarios.name: battle_safari
scenarios.verification: battle plan 4d's witness: the first scenario to RENDER the Safari battle menu. Compares the tilemap, because what the Safari branches produce IS the screen -- the SAFARI_BATTLE_MENU_TEMPLATE full-width box, the BALL/BAIT/THROW ROCK/RUN labels, the two Safari cursor columns (pret ld b,$1 and ld b,$d) and the remaining-ball counter (pret hlcoord 7,14 + PrintNumber). wBattleType is pinned EARLY and every frame: late, the ROM sends the player's mon out and the two sides photograph different phases (pret StartBattle:171 skips the send-out for any non-zero wBattleType). wNumSafariBalls is pinned to 30 because the menu PRINTS it into the compared tilemap. scenarios.name: battle_safari_result
scenarios.verification: The RESULT/EXIT half of the per-battle-type box for SAFARI, and the first scenario ever to execute production's _InitBattleCommon.specialBattleLoop -- measured 2026-08-14 with four in-WRAM markers, that loop (the out-of-balls exit, PrintSafariZoneBattleText and the flee roll) was entered by NO scenario, because battle_safari's gate calls DisplayBattleMenu directly. BAIT is chosen, not BALL: a ball attempts a catch (a roll) and a success exits through UseBagItem's carry return before the tail runs at all. THE FLEE IS RNG-FREE RATHER THAN SEEDED, which is what makes this deterministic across two emulators that share no RNG stream -- pret core.asm:189-192 opens `ld a,[wEnemyMonSpeed+1] / add a / jp c, EnemyRan`, so a speed LOW byte (big-endian, so +1) above 127 runs the mon outright BEFORE Random is called; both sides pin it to $80. LANDMARK is the enemy pic GONE *and* "ran!" on the tilemap, and both halves are required: "ran!" alone fires during PrintText, before pret's `jpfar AnimationSlideEnemyMonOff` tail, at which instant the two sides disagree about the pic band by construction. THE GATE ORDER MATTERS: this build also defines DEBUG_BATTLE_SAFARI, so its build_flags must carry MORE tokens than battle_safari's two or the registry's descending-token %ifdef chain stamps id 71 -- which is exactly what the pre-registration dump reported.

scenarios.name: battle_run_type
scenarios.verification: The LAST battle type in box 2225. BATTLE_TYPE_RUN is unused in the shipped game, so its arms were faithful but reachable by nothing. THE PLAN RECORDED THIS AS BLOCKED ON CROSS-EMULATOR STAGING AND THAT DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG: the earlier attempt pinned wBattleAndStartSavedMenuItem, but pret's .handleUnusedBattle reads wCurrentMenuItem (core.asm:2257), so the pin never selected RUN and the arm did what pret says it does for every OTHER selection -- print "Hurry, get away!" and redraw the menu. Real key presses fix it and no menu pin is needed. NAVIGATION read out of pret: the battle menu builds wCurrentMenuItem as ROW plus 2 if in the RIGHT COLUMN (core.asm:2215-2217), so RUN is row 1 + column 2 = item 3, i.e. DOWN then RIGHT. IT IS RNG-FREE, which is what makes it comparable: TryRunningFromBattle tests `cp BATTLE_TYPE_RUN / jp z, .canEscape` BEFORE the speed comparison and before Random is called, so the run always succeeds. BATTLE_TYPE_RUN also reaches the SAME special-battle loop as SAFARI -- pret .checkAnyPartyAlive sends it to .specialBattle, which falls into .displaySafariZoneBattleMenu because wBattleType is non-zero -- so the port gate enters through the trampoline battle_safari_result added. LANDMARK is "Got away safely!" on the tilemap AND wIsInBattle back to 0: the text alone would catch the message mid-battle, while the port gate's call returns only after .battleFinished has run EndOfBattle, so both sides land POST-TEARDOWN.

scenarios.name: battle_ai_switch
scenarios.verification: Battle plan 1e's witness: the trainer AI CHOOSING TO SWITCH. SwitchEnemyMon has exactly one caller (AISwitchIfEnoughMons) and until 2026-08-14 NOTHING in the suite reached it, which is why the 2026-08-11 defect -- the routine copied the withdrawn mon's HP back to the roster and NEVER SENT THE REPLACEMENT OUT -- could not have been caught by any gate then in existence. Entry is trainer_battle_route's real Route 3 sight battle against OPP_BUG_CATCHER party 4 (CATERPIE/WEEDLE/CATERPIE L10, three mons, over AISwitchIfEnoughMons' `cp 2`). TWO STAGING WRITES, deliberately asymmetric: wTrainerClass = COOLTRAINER_F every frame (safe, nothing animates toward it, and it is the ONLY RNG-free route to the switch because pret COMMENTED OUT the `ret nc` after that class's `cp 25 percent + 1`, so it alone ignores TrainerAI's Random byte); and wEnemyMonHP SEEDED ONCE into CooltrainerFAI's band maxHP/10 <= HP < maxHP/5, COMPUTED from the maxHP read, then never touched again. THE SEED MUST NOT BECOME A PER-FRAME PIN -- measured twice, a per-frame HP write stalls the flow SILENTLY because anything animating toward a target HP cannot converge. THE SEED FIRES ON A STATE, NOT A FRAME COUNT: wBattleMonSpecies becoming non-zero (the player send-out completing). A frame delay does NOT align the two emulators -- measured, the reference's A-tap cadence advances the battle faster than the port's AUTOKEY_TRAINER_ROUTE, so at a fixed delay the two sides seeded different mons. One seed suffices because the debug lead SNORLAX L80's move slot 0 is FLY, a TWO-TURN move: turn 1 is the charge, so the enemy survives to be consulted -- unlike trainer_battle_route this scenario must NOT select STRENGTH by name. LANDMARK: wEnemyMonPartyPos in 1..5, a replacement loaded, AND eRoster1HP NON-ZERO. The roster HP is what separates a SWITCH from a FAINT and leaving it out photographed the wrong event: the first golden caught WEEDLE at partyPos 1 with eRoster1HP 0000, the faint path, while the port had genuinely switched.

scenarios.name: surfing_pikachu_intro
scenarios.verification: backlog item 34 / archived docs/plans/surfing_pikachu.md Stage 8, defending the two rendering defects fixed 2026-08-18 (7445a3fa8): no OBJ ever drawn on this screen (g_obj_over_window zeroed by ClearSprites) and the intro rendering as a uniform tile-$00 field (nothing mirrored wTileMap to GB_TILEMAP0). Entry is FORCED and SYMMETRIC with the port's RunSurfingPikachuTest debug gate (maintainer directive): seed.debug_new_game byte-for-byte matches PrepareNewGameDebug's party/bag/pokedex/money/badges, wPikachuSpawnStateFlags BIT_PIKACHU_SPAWN_SURFING is seeded to bypass the NPC's own precondition, and the golden reaches the SAME farcall SurfingPikachuMinigame the port gate calls directly -- but through the real in-game dispatch (a script-warp next to the Summer Beach House's Surfin' Dude NPC, then two real button presses through the actual SummerBeachHouseSurfinDudeText script), not by skipping it. RNG (SurfingMinigame_ChooseNextWaveSequence) and the 3-frame-buffered joypad make the gameplay loop cross-emulator uncomparable, so this witnesses only SurfingPikachuMinigameIntro, whose background draw has no RNG and no input read. Checkpoint is content-based (wTileMap fully drawn), not frame-count based: a sentinel ($FF) is seeded into wSurfingMinigameIntroAnimationFinished, polled until pret's own `xor a / ld [wSurfingMinigameIntroAnimationFinished], a` overwrites it with 0 immediately before `.loop:`, then exactly one loop iteration (one DelayFrame) is let run so OAM is published once by RunObjectAnimations before the intro Pikachu's own per-2-frame step has moved it from its spawn X -- so OAM position is compared with no frame-alignment slack needed. Measured deterministic: two independent mGBA runs produced a byte-identical golden .bin/.json.
